analysis.investment_thesis: Asahi India Glass trades at P/E 69.2 and P/B 5.86 — levels that price in years of flawless execution with zero allowance for adversity. A business earning ₹367 Cr net profit on a ₹21,701 Cr market cap offers a 1.7% earnings yield, far below what any prudent investor should accept when government bonds offer multiples of that risk-free.
key_strengths: Dominant position in Indian automotive glass with both OEM and aftermarket channels providing revenue diversification
Operating CF positive all five years; interest coverage of ~6x (EBITDA ₹782 Cr / finance cost ₹128 Cr) remains adequate
Long-run net profit CAGR of 17.6% over nine years demonstrates genuine earnings growth capacity
key_risks: D/E of 0.77 breaches my 0.5 threshold; borrowings surged from ₹1,238 Cr (FY2022) to ₹2,856 Cr (FY2025) as capex expanded aggressively
Free cash flow turned deeply negative: -₹244 Cr (FY2024) and -₹536 Cr (FY2025) — the company is consuming capital faster than it generates it
Automotive glass is a cyclical, capital-intensive commodity business with limited pricing power; any auto-cycle downturn compresses margins sharply
red_flags: P/E of 69.2 is nearly 5x my maximum acceptable ratio of 15 — the stock is priced for perfection, not value
P/B of 5.86 means investors pay ₹5.86 for every ₹1 of net assets — liquidation value provides zero protection
Escalating debt (borrowings up 131% in three years) combined with mounting capex and negative FCF is exactly the leverage trap I warn against
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Graham Number for Asahi India is not computable at a sensible level — with a P/B near 6 and P/E near 70, the stock would need to fall roughly 80% to approach the kind of asset-backed valuation I consider. EV/EBITDA of 31.9 confirms the same verdict from a different angle. The FY2025 negative FCF of -₹536 Cr alongside total debt of ₹2,696 Cr tells me that the company's growth is being funded by creditors, not by the business itself.

The business has genuine merit — a near-duopoly in Indian automotive glass, good gross margins (65%), and a long earnings history. But Mr. Market is pricing all of that in and then some. I am not in the business of paying for other people's optimism. Until this stock trades at a P/E below 15 and a P/B below 1.5 — implying a price well under ₹200 — I will not touch it.
